observation.visible_scene: A wooden/bamboo tea tray engraved with vertical columns of Chinese characters holds three small white porcelain tasting cups arranged in a diagonal row, a clear glass pitcher (fair cup) at the upper right, and a leaf-shaped ceramic dish of dry tea leaves at the lower left. Dark-clothed knees of a seated person are visible at the top left, and a bamboo tool lies at the top right edge. A thin stream of water falls from above into the glass pitcher.
visible_changes: Water continues to be poured into the glass pitcher throughout the segment; the incoming stream is visible at the pitcher's rim in most frames.
The liquid level inside the pitcher gradually rises and the contents swirl, with the pitcher appearing fuller and more uniformly filled by the last frames compared to the first.
Faint vertical wisps/streaks appear intermittently just above the pitcher (likely steam or falling droplets).
The three white cups remain empty and unmoved; the tea-leaf dish and the seated person's posture stay unchanged.
The camera is stationary; the tray, cups, dish, and background do not shift relative to the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: The source of the pouring stream (a kettle or vessel held above the frame) is not visible.
Whether the pouring stops or the pitcher overflows after the last frame is unknown.
The state of the scene before the first frame (how full the pitcher started) is not shown.
uncertain_details: The thin vertical marks above the pitcher could be steam, a broken water stream, or droplets; their exact nature is unclear.
The magnitude of the water-level rise is subtle and partly obscured by reflections and refraction in the glass.
